title: Latin American Studies since the 1980s: From Apocalyptic Dreams to Assimilationist Consolidation
abstract: arXiv:2611.13216v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We investigate how Latin American Studies (LAS) has evolved since 1982 in three leading LAS journals. Using network analysis, text mining, and bibliometrics, we trace transformations in disciplinary positioning, authorship, and citation patterns. Our main claim is that LAS has undergone an assimilationist consolidation. The field is now institutionally recognisable, with core LAS journals occupying central positions in disciplinary networks and acting as bridges across fields. Yet this consolidation has reinforced hierarchies privileging Anglophone academic norms. Journals based in Latin America, once central, have been marginalised. The share of Latin American authors has grown, but their profiles converge towards Northern standards.

translated_title: 20世纪80年代以来的拉丁美洲研究：从末世梦魇到同化式整合
translated_abstract: 我们研究了拉丁美洲研究（LAS）自1982年以来在三本顶级LAS期刊中的演变历程。通过网络分析、文本挖掘和文献计量学方法，我们追踪了该领域在学科定位、作者构成和引用模式上的变迁。我们的核心论点是：拉丁美洲研究经历了一场“同化式整合”。该领域如今已获得制度层面的认可，核心LAS期刊在学科网络中占据中心位置，并在各学科之间充当桥梁。然而，这种整合也强化了偏向英语学术规范的等级体系。曾经处于中心地位的拉丁美洲本土期刊已被边缘化；拉丁美洲作者的比例虽有所增长，但其学术特征正日益趋同于北方（英美）标准。
tldr: 该研究通过文献计量学揭示了拉丁美洲研究自1982年以来的“同化式整合”趋势——学科制度化地位提升的同时，却强化了以英语学术规范为主导的等级体系，导致拉美本土期刊边缘化和拉美学者向北方标准的趋同。
